Polyisocyanurate (polyiso) roof insulation boards consist of a rigid closed-cell foam core sandwiched between two facers (top and bottom). The foam core is a thermoset polymer produced through the reaction of methylene diphenylene diisocyanate (MDI) with polyester polyol, along with additives such as catalyst, surfactant, flame retardant, and blowing agent (pentane or pentane blends). For roofing applications, the most common facer is a glass fiber reinforced cellulosic facer (GRF) produced predominantly from recycled post-consumer and/or post-industrial fibers. Polyiso roof insulation is also manufactured with polymer-bonded coated glass facer (CGF), consisting of a glass fiber mat coated with polymers. Polyiso is the most widely used type of insulation in above-deck commercial roof applications in the United States and Canada. It is compatible with all low-slope roof covering types including single-ply membranes, modified bitumen systems, built-up roofing, standing-seam metal roofing, and metal panels. It is characterized by high thermal resistance, lightweight construction, and direct-to-steel deck application without a thermal barrier.
